sentences.text:
THE APPEAL AND CROSS OBJECTION, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

The appeal in M.F.A. No.100157/2021 is filed by the insurer against the judgment and award dated 30th May 2020 passed in M.V.C. No.1105/2018 by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi (for short, 'the Tribunal').
The cross-objection is filed by the claimant against the very same impugned judgment and award.
2. The cross-objector is seeking enhancement of the compensation.
The appellant-insurer is seeking reduction of the compensation.
3. The accident is not in dispute.
The liability is also not in dispute.

4. The appellant-insurer is before this Court on the premise that the assessment of disability at 20%
by the Tribunal is on the higher side as the doctor has assessed the disability to the lower limb at 30% and he would submit that 10% disability ought to have been taken by the Tribunal.

Looking to the nature of the injury, the disability, the evidence on record and also the avocation of the claimant,
this Court is of the view that the Tribunal has erred in taking 20% as the disability to assess the 'loss of future income' and the disability is to be taken at 10%.
Accordingly, the compensation under the said head has to be re-assessed.
5. In the absence of any proof relating to income, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the claimant as Rs.9,000/- per month.

Since the chart prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority is the guiding factor in the absence of proof of income relating to income, by referring to the same, this Court is of the view that the notional income of the claimant is to be taken at Rs.11,750/- per month as the accident is of the year 2018.
As such the compensation is to be re-determined.
6. Since the notional income is revised and also the disability is reassessed, the loss of future income would be Rs.1,83,300/- [Rs.11,750 x 12(months) x 10%(disability) x 13(multiplier)].

7. On re-assessment, the claimant is entitled to the modified compensation as under:
1) Loss of income due to disability Rs. 1,83,300/-
2) Pain and suffering Rs. 25,000/-
 3) Medical expenses Rs. 36,000/-
 4) Food and nourishment Rs. 3,000/-
 5) Attendant charges Rs. 2,000/-
 6) Travelling expenses Rs. 2,000/-
 7) Loss of earning during laid up  period Rs. 35,250/-
 8) Loss of amenities in life Rs. 25,000/-
 TOTAL Rs. 3,11,550/-
Thus, the cross-objector/claimant is held entitled to a reduced compensation of Rs.3,11,550/-, as against Rs.4,08,800/- awarded by the Tribunal.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum.

8. Hence, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal filed by the appellant-insurer is allowed in part.
(ii) The cross-objection filed by the cross- objector/claimant is dismissed.
(iii) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal are modified.
The cross- objector/claimant is entitled to compensation of Rs.3,11,550/- with interest at the rate of 6% per annum.
(iv) The appellant-insurer to deposit the reduced compensation amount along with interest within six weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this order.

The amount in deposit, if any, before this Court is ordered to be transmitted to the Tribunal concerned Sd/-
